currentContext.expansion: The annual report discloses no new plant, greenfield project, brownfield line or capex programme with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Growth for FY2026-27 is planned entirely out of headroom in the existing facility: the MD&A Outlook states the Company has a normal capacity of producing 25,000 pieces of lenses per day against an installed capacity of manufacturing 35,000 lenses per day, and that having manufactured 34,88,865 pieces in the year ended March 31, 2026 it expects to increase this by 40% in the current financial year given demand, alongside a targeted sale of Rs. 36.00 Crores. The only structural 'footprint' developments disclosed are contractions rather than expansions: Prime Ophthalmics Products PTY Limited, the South African trading subsidiary of GKB Ophthalmics Products FZE, is undergoing closure after difficulties recruiting a competent management team and an inability to generate sufficient sales, and GSV Ophthalmics Private Limited, a material subsidiary inoperative since inception, is under voluntary liquidation under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, with the Company having received back from GSV its equity share capital investment during the year. Commercial effort is directed at expanding the domestic customer base and at pursuing anti-dumping duties on plastic lens imports rather than at adding capacity.

risks.risk: Import dumping from China at prices below cost
risks.note: MD&A 'Opportunities and Threats' and the Board's Report both state the business faces stiff competition from China, with Chinese manufacturers dumping ophthalmic lenses in India at very low / below-cost prices. Management says this has created significant pressure on domestic pricing and margins and has resulted in reduced market share and lower sales realisation. The remedy the Company won - anti-dumping duty on semi-finished lenses from China PR under Notification No. 32/2022-Customs (ADD) dated December 27, 2022, effective for five years - is considered by the Company itself to provide insufficient remedy, and it has gone for an appeal, so the outcome is unresolved.

risks.risk: US tariff and trade-restriction exposure on exports
risks.note: MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' states that during the year the imposition of high tariffs by the US Government significantly impacted exports to the subsidiary Lensco - The Lens Company, New Jersey. The Board's Report adds that increased tariffs and trade restrictions imposed by the US government affected export competitiveness and demand in international markets. Recovery in FY2026-27 is explicitly conditioned on 'tariffs returning to normal levels', a variable outside the Company's control.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange fluctuation and dependence on export-country economies
risks.note: The only risk management explicitly acknowledges in MD&A: 'We do not foresee any risks, except for foreign exchange fluctuations.' Because the Company depends on exports, the economic situation in exporting countries is stated as likely to affect performance - so both the currency and the destination-market cycle sit directly on results.

risks.risk: Imported raw-material dependence and supply-chain friction
risks.note: MD&A states the market remains heavily reliant on imported raw materials, with 65% of lens materials sourced internationally, and that this dependency, coupled with customs clearance delays and internal transportation challenges, continues to impact product availability across urban and rural regions. This compounds the forex exposure on the input side of the same P&L already exposed on the export side.

MD&A 'Segment wise or Product wise Performance' says only that the Company is engaged in the business of manufacturing semi-finished plastic lenses. There is no second product line or segment to absorb a shock in lens pricing or lens demand, so the China-dumping and US-tariff pressures hit the entire business at once.

risks.risk: Scale disadvantage against dominant international lens manufacturers
risks.note: MD&A states that domestic manufacturers face significant hurdles in expanding their business due to the dominance of international plastic lens manufacturers, and that growth of the local market is hampered by intense competition from low-cost imported lenses - a structural constraint on the very domestic-customer-base expansion the Company is relying on for recovery.

risks.risk: Unresolved labour litigation and a Labour Commissioner recovery order
risks.note: Under 'Significant and Material Orders Passed by the Regulators', the Board's Report discloses an Industrial Tribunal Panjim-Goa Award dated 25/05/2021 in Case no. 32/09 (Charter of Demands filed in 2009 by the Workmen represented by the Goa Trade & Commercial Workers' Union), which the Company is challenging by writ petition. On September 12, 2025 the Labour Commissioner ordered recovery from the Company for execution of that Award; the Company is not admitting the liability and is challenging the Order before the Hon'ble High Court. This is a live contingent claim in a labour-intensive business against a loss-making standalone entity.

risks.risk: Internal-control observation on electronic back-up of books of account
risks.note: Although the Auditors' Report is unmodified with no qualifications, reservations or adverse remarks, the Board responds to the auditors' Paragraph 2(b) observation that for records maintained by the inventory management software the electronic back-up of books and accounts is not being maintained on a daily basis. Remediation is stated as ongoing coordination between the concerned department and the technical team - a books-and-records control gap that remains open at the reporting date.
